the effects of gluino-mediated supersymmetric contributions are small for the constrained LL and constrained RR mass insertions but can be sizable for the constrained LR mass insertions in the decays of B_s-> K^{(*)-}{K^{(*)+}}.

the gluino-mediated contributions to the observables of B_{s}\to\bar{K}^{(*)0}K^{(*)-}, B_{s}\rightarrow\bar{K^{0}}K^{0} and B\rightarrow X_s \gamma decays are sizable in the frame of constrained MSSM and can be constrained by current and future experiments.

the study of B_s-\bar{B_s} mixing and B_s->K^-K^+ decay within supersymmetry and its phenomenological implications.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the current experimental data on the B_s system can not be explained within the MSSM.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the supersymmetry contributions can provide a large CP asymmetries and a large branching ratios for B_s^0->K^{-}pi^{+} and B_s^0 -> K^{-}K^{*0} decays.

supersymmetry can explain the recent CDF and D0 measurements on B_s^0 - \bar{B}_0s mixing and B_s->K^{-+} decays, and the mass insertion parameter can be probed by the future experiments at FermiLab Tevatron and LHC-b at CERN.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the supersymmetric contributions are not negligible, and the supersymmetric effects may be important in the future experiments at Tevatron and LHC-b.
B_s->K^+K^- and B_s->K^{-}\Kp^{+} decays provide a complementary way to probe the LR mass insertion, while the standard B_s->J/\psi\Phi decay can only test the LR mass insertion with a large phase.
